summary: AI adoption is in extremely early innings globally; compute shortage exists with only ~500K people using generative AI out of 8 billion
summary_extended: Baker argues that AI adoption is in the earliest possible innings globally, citing an estimate from 'Yoc' that only approximately 500,000 people worldwide are currently using generative AI out of a global population of 8 billion. He reasons that even reaching 1% global adoption — 80 million users — would require orders-of-magnitude more compute than currently exists, and the world is already experiencing an acute compute shortage at the current negligible adoption level. This structural supply-demand imbalance forms Baker's foundational long-term bull case for AI infrastructure investment, suggesting that demand for compute will compound dramatically for years. The investment implication is a sustained, multi-year tailwind for AI infrastructure providers, particularly those supplying the compute hardware and data center capacity required to scale from hundreds of thousands to hundreds of millions or billions of AI users.
detail: Baker cites an estimate (attributed to 'Yoc') that only ~500,000 people globally are using generative AI, and the world is already in an acute compute shortage. Going from 500K to 1% of 8 billion (80M) or beyond implies orders-of-magnitude more compute demand. This is the structural long-term bull case for AI infrastructure.
